skills.name: code-review
skills.description: Reviews a diff, pull request, or set of staged changes for correctness, tests, error and edge cases, security, performance, readability, and architectural fit, then reports severity-ranked, actionable findings with file and line references. Use when reviewing a PR, examining staged or unstaged changes, giving feedback on a patch, or deciding whether a change is safe to merge.

inputs.description: A branch, pull request, or set of staged or unstaged changes.

outputs.description: Severity-ranked, actionable findings with file and line references.

examplePrompts: Review this pull request for correctness and regressions.
Inspect my staged changes and report only actionable findings.

skills.name: codebase-exploration
skills.description: Builds a focused, evidence-based map of an unfamiliar repository before modifying it, locating entry points, build, test, and lint commands, architecture boundaries, conventions, the dependency graph, and the nearest agent instructions, then reading tests to learn intended behavior and finding the smallest correct change site. Use when onboarding to a new or unfamiliar codebase, orienting before a change, or answering how a project is structured and where to edit, while staying read-only.

inputs.description: An unfamiliar repository or component to map before modification.

outputs.description: An evidence-based map of entry points, commands, boundaries, and change sites.

examplePrompts: Map this repository before we change the authentication flow.
Find the entry points, test commands, and smallest correct edit location.

skills.name: copilot-cloud-agent
skills.description: Launches and monitors GitHub Copilot cloud-agent tasks through supported GitHub APIs, selecting explicit models, recording task and pull-request IDs, and distinguishing hosted controls from local CLI flags. Use when starting cloud agents, running hosted loops, assigning issues to Copilot, choosing GPT-5.6 Sol, or checking cloud-agent status; do not use for local subagents or git worktree fleets.

inputs.description: A repository, bounded prompt, base ref, pull-request preference, and optional hosted model.

outputs.description: A verified hosted task with task, session, model, branch, and pull-request metadata.

runtimeCompatibility.notes: Requires authenticated access to GitHub's cloud-agent API.
Requires authenticated access to GitHub's cloud-agent API.
Requires authenticated access to GitHub's cloud-agent API.

examplePrompts: Launch a GitHub Copilot cloud agent with GPT-5.6 Sol and create a pull request.
Check which model this hosted Copilot task used and report its current state.

skills.name: documentation-maintenance
skills.description: Keeps README, API docs, architecture notes, ADRs, and changelogs accurate when code changes by identifying which documents a change invalidates, documenting rationale, keeping setup instructions and examples runnable, updating the changelog with user-visible changes, and removing stale content. Use when code, configuration, commands, interfaces, or behavior change and documentation must be updated, or when writing an ADR or changelog entry.

inputs.description: A code, configuration, command, interface, or behavior change.
A request for an ADR, changelog entry, or documentation repair.

outputs.description: Accurate, runnable documentation aligned with current behavior.

examplePrompts: Update the README and changelog for this command change.
Write an ADR for the new persistence boundary.

skills.name: external-skill-review
skills.description: Reviews third-party agent skills as untrusted code before installing or updating them, assessing provenance, license, the full file tree, scripts, hidden Unicode, network and secret access, destructive commands, tool permissions, and supply-chain risk. Use when installing, updating, vetting, or auditing an external skill, a gh skill install candidate, or any skill from an untrusted repository.

inputs.description: A third-party skill directory or installation candidate.

outputs.description: A provenance and supply-chain assessment with an install recommendation.

examplePrompts: Audit this third-party skill before I install it.
Review this gh skill install candidate for supply-chain risk.

skills.name: git-and-pr-workflow
skills.description: Guides Git branching, atomic commits, rebasing, resolving merge conflicts, worktrees, pull request descriptions, and safely finishing a branch. Use when creating branches, staging and committing changes, rebasing or squashing, resolving conflicts, opening or updating a pull request, or cleaning up after merge.

inputs.description: A repository with changes to branch, commit, rebase, or submit.

outputs.description: A reviewable branch, atomic commit history, or pull request.

examplePrompts: Create an atomic commit and open a pull request for these changes.
Safely rebase my unshared branch and resolve its conflicts.

skills.name: parallel-worktree-delivery
skills.description: Executes multi-agent, multi-branch git worktree delivery with ownership partitions, dependency waves, branch integration, merge conflict handling, and post-merge gates. Use when running worktree fleets, integration branches, or wave-based migrations where checkout collisions are a risk; do not use merely to identify parallel tasks or for a single small change.

inputs.description: A dependency-aware plan with safely partitioned file ownership.

outputs.description: A verified integration branch assembled from isolated worktree changes.

examplePrompts: Deliver this migration with parallel agents in isolated worktrees.
Coordinate dependency waves and integrate each branch safely.

skills.name: planning-and-task-breakdown
skills.description: Decomposes an approved specification into small, ordered, dependency-aware tasks, each with explicit acceptance criteria and a verification command, and identifies which tasks are independent and safely parallelizable without overlapping writes. Use when planning multi-step work, breaking a spec or feature into tasks, sequencing dependencies, or coordinating parallel agents, after requirements are agreed and before implementation begins.

inputs.description: An agreed specification or clearly bounded implementation request.

outputs.description: Ordered, dependency-aware tasks with acceptance criteria and verification commands.

examplePrompts: Break this approved specification into implementation tasks.
Sequence this migration and identify safely parallel work.

skills.name: refactoring-and-dead-code-removal
skills.description: Changes code structure without changing behavior and removes unused code safely by establishing a passing baseline, making one mechanical change at a time, re-running tests between steps, and proving code is dead before deleting it. Use when cleaning up, simplifying, restructuring, extracting, renaming, or deleting suspected unused code, imports, functions, or files.

inputs.description: Code to restructure, simplify, rename, or prove unused.

outputs.description: A behavior-preserving structural change with dead code safely removed.

examplePrompts: Extract this module without changing behavior.
Prove this helper is unused and remove it safely.

skills.name: repository-agent-bootstrap
skills.description: Audits and bootstraps repository-owned agent customization including AGENTS.md, repository and path-scoped instructions, custom agents, and skills, without overwriting established conventions. Use to set up, review, or maintain a repository's agent guidance, add a skill or agent, or fix overlapping, stale, or overly broad customization.

inputs.description: A repository that needs agent instructions, profiles, or skills.

outputs.description: A minimal repository-owned agent customization structure and its files.

examplePrompts: Bootstrap AGENTS.md and repository-owned skills for this project.
Audit our agent customization and fill the smallest useful gaps.

skills.name: requirements-and-spec-writing
skills.description: Turns an ambiguous or large request into an agreed written specification before implementation, covering objective, users and use cases, requirements, non-goals, interfaces and data contracts, security and privacy, error and edge cases, acceptance criteria, open questions, alternatives considered, and rollout and rollback. Use when a request is vague, scope or acceptance criteria are unclear, or the user asks for a spec, requirements, or a design before coding begins.

inputs.description: An ambiguous or large feature, behavior, or design request.

outputs.description: An agreed specification with requirements, boundaries, interfaces, and rollout.

examplePrompts: Turn this feature idea into an implementation-ready specification.
Define requirements, non-goals, edge cases, and acceptance criteria.

skills.name: security-review
skills.description: Performs threat-focused security review of a code change or component using STRIDE, checking authentication, authorization and ownership, input validation, injection, deserialization, SSRF, secrets handling, dependency and supply-chain risk, cryptography, and untrusted data including prompt injection. Use when reviewing a diff, feature, endpoint, or integration for vulnerabilities, threat modeling, or hardening before merge or release.

inputs.description: A code change, endpoint, feature, or integration to review for vulnerabilities.

outputs.description: Severity-ranked vulnerabilities, threat scenarios, and concrete mitigations.

examplePrompts: Threat-model this new webhook endpoint.
Review this authentication change for exploitable vulnerabilities.

skills.name: shadow-architecture
skills.description: Sets up and maintains a repository-owned .shadow graph, manages approved decision lifecycles and index or schema compatibility, supersedes accepted history, and renders reviewed records. Use when creating or migrating .shadow, recording approved architecture decisions, maintaining its index or schema, superseding accepted decisions, or generating derived views from reviewed records; not for discovering observations, imagining future states, or checking drift.

inputs.description: A .shadow graph or human-approved architecture decision to record, maintain, supersede, or render.

outputs.description: A maintained evidence-linked .shadow graph or derived view of reviewed records.

examplePrompts: Record this human-approved architecture decision in the .shadow graph.
Migrate this .shadow graph to the v2 contract without rewriting accepted history.

skills.name: shadow-dream
skills.description: Generates evidence-linked future-state architecture options and a reviewable proposal from Shadow observations and accepted constraints, including target states, tradeoffs, migration paths, rollback, risks, and a recommendation. Use when asked to dream, explore architecture options, compare future-state architecture, define a target state, or propose a migration path; excludes product requirements and specifications handled by requirements-and-spec-writing and implementation task planning handled by planning-and-task-breakdown.

inputs.description: Evidence-linked current-state observations and accepted constraints for a future-state architecture question.

outputs.description: Reviewable future-state options, tradeoffs, recommendation, migration stages, rollback, and approval gate.

examplePrompts: Dream two future-state architectures from these Shadow observations and compare their migration risks.
Propose a target architecture and rollback path without treating it as approved.

skills.name: shadow-drift
skills.description: Checks repository-owned .shadow decision graphs read-only, validates architecture drift, stale decisions, relations, evidence, indexes, and derived output, and reports aligned, drifted, stale, and unknown findings. Use when asked to check Shadow, validate .shadow, investigate architecture drift, or identify stale decisions; not for general completion verification, pull-request review, documentation maintenance, observation capture, speculative architecture, or repairing the graph.

inputs.description: A repository-owned .shadow graph and current implementation evidence to validate read-only.

outputs.description: Evidence-linked aligned, drifted, stale, unknown, and graph-integrity findings.

examplePrompts: Check this .shadow graph for architecture drift without repairing it.
Validate decision relations, evidence, and derived output against the implementation.

skills.name: shadow-observe
skills.description: Runs bounded, read-only Shadow repository analysis to generate evidence-linked candidate architecture observations, map boundaries and dependencies, and separate verified claims, inference, and unknowns. Use when asked to run Shadow, scan architecture, generate observations, or map boundaries or dependencies for a repository-owned .shadow graph; unlike codebase-exploration, it does not orient an unfamiliar codebase or locate change sites, and it does not create decisions, propose future state, or repair drift.

inputs.description: A bounded repository scope and architecture question for read-only current-state analysis.

outputs.description: Evidence-linked candidate observations separated into verified claims, inferences, and unknowns.

examplePrompts: Run Shadow on the authentication boundary and return candidate observations.
Map current API and persistence dependencies without creating decisions.

skills.name: skill-creator
skills.description: Creates, audits, and improves Agent Skills in this catalog. Captures intent, triggers, and outputs, checks the catalog for overlap, drafts positive and negative trigger prompts, writes routing descriptions, applies progressive disclosure, decides prose versus script, and validates frontmatter. Use when authoring a new SKILL.md, editing or reviewing an existing skill, fixing a skill that fails validation or fails to trigger, or when someone mentions skill authoring, skill frontmatter, or the skill catalog.

inputs.description: A capability, realistic trigger requests, or an existing skill to improve.

outputs.description: A validated portable skill directory with reliable routing metadata.

examplePrompts: Create a portable skill for database migration reviews.
Audit this SKILL.md and improve its routing description.

skills.name: systematic-debugging
skills.description: Diagnoses bugs, failing tests, build failures, crashes, exceptions, stack traces, and unexpected or intermittent behavior by reproducing the failure, capturing exact error output, isolating the root cause, and fixing the cause rather than the symptom. Use when something is broken, a test or build fails, output is wrong, or a defect must be traced to its origin.

inputs.description: A bug, failing test, build error, crash, or unexpected behavior.

outputs.description: A reproduced diagnosis and verified fix for the underlying cause.

examplePrompts: Reproduce and fix this intermittent test failure.
Trace this exception to its root cause instead of patching the symptom.

skills.name: test-driven-development
skills.description: Drives implementation with the red-green-refactor cycle by writing a failing behavior test first, confirming it fails for the expected reason, implementing the minimum code to pass, then refactoring while green. Use when adding a feature, fixing a bug with a reproducible case, changing behavior, or whenever tests should precede or guide the implementation.

inputs.description: A feature or reproducible bug whose behavior can be tested first.

outputs.description: A minimal implementation developed through a demonstrated red-green-refactor cycle.

examplePrompts: Add this behavior using red-green-refactor.
Write a failing regression test before fixing this bug.

skills.name: verification-before-completion
skills.description: Requires fresh evidence before any claim that work is done, fixed, passing, working, complete, or ready. Run the relevant command now, read the actual output and exit status, inspect the produced artifact or diff, reproduce the original symptom and confirm it is gone, and distinguish verified results from assumed ones. Use before reporting completion, closing a task, or telling the user something works, and whenever tests, builds, or lint results are described as passing.

inputs.description: A claim that work is fixed, passing, ready, or complete.

outputs.description: Fresh command or artifact evidence supporting or rejecting the claim.

examplePrompts: Verify this fix is actually complete before reporting success.
Run the relevant checks and distinguish verified results from assumptions.

skills.name: verification-discipline
skills.description: Audits and hardens existing tests and validation so green results are meaningful by detecting vacuous assertions, copied production logic, unbounded checks, unenforced invariants, and build impurity. Use when reviewing suspicious green tests, repairing test credibility, or hardening CI gates; do not use for ordinary test-first feature implementation or routine final gate selection.

inputs.description: Tests or CI validation whose green result may be weak or misleading.

outputs.description: A hardened validation design with credible assertions and enforced invariants.

examplePrompts: Audit these suspiciously green tests for vacuous assertions.
Harden this CI gate so it enforces the intended invariant.

skills.name: web-research-and-verification
skills.description: Answers questions that depend on current external information by detecting the exact version in use, preferring primary and authoritative sources, corroborating with a second source, quoting and citing URLs, and separating verified fact from inference. Use when researching APIs, libraries, standards, release notes, CVEs, or any claim where accuracy and up-to-date sourcing matter, or when a source may be deprecated.

inputs.description: A question that depends on current external APIs, releases, standards, or vulnerabilities.

outputs.description: A source-backed answer separating verified facts from inference.

examplePrompts: Research the current API behavior and cite primary sources.
Verify whether this dependency version is affected by the latest CVE.

packs.name: feature-delivery
packs.description: Carries an agreed feature from requirements through implementation review, documentation, and completion verification.

handoffs.when: The approved work is decomposed into ordered tasks with acceptance criteria.
The implementation has completed its red-green-refactor cycle.
The implementation review has no unresolved required findings.
Directly affected documentation and changelog entries are current.

packs.name: release-readiness
packs.description: Coordinates correctness, security, documentation, and final evidence checks before release-related Git work.

handoffs.when: Functional review has no unresolved required findings.
Security review has no unresolved required findings.
Release-facing documentation and changelog entries are current.
Fresh validation evidence supports release readiness.

packs.name: safe-refactor
packs.description: Guides a behavior-preserving refactor from codebase mapping and tests through review and completion verification.

handoffs.when: The controlling code path, conventions, and validation commands are known.
A failing behavior test establishes the preservation boundary.
The mechanical refactor is complete with behavior tests passing.
The refactor review has no unresolved required findings.

packs.name: shadow-architecture-suite
packs.description: Carries a full Shadow architecture lifecycle from current-state observations through approved decision recording and read-only drift validation.

handoffs.when: Candidate observations are ready for future-state exploration.
A human has explicitly approved the future-state proposal for decision recording.
Architecture decisions and implementation are updated and ready for read-only drift validation.
